finding.claim: validateRealm only blocks private/loopback/link-local/unspecified targets when the realm host is an IP literal, so a registry-supplied bearer realm naming localhost, an internal DNS name, or a host resolving to a metadata/private address is accepted. The client then sends a GET (with Basic creds if configured) or a password-grant POST to that host.
finding.source: Www-Authenticate realm parameter from the registry's 401 response (client.go:309-310, challenge.go:67-132), read at client.go:356
finding.sink: fetchDistributionToken GET with SetBasicAuth (client.go:417-434) and fetchOAuth2Token POST (client.go:488-494)

trace.note: parseChallenge extracts realm param from Www-Authenticate
Do reads Www-Authenticate from the 401 response
IP-literal-only private/loopback check; net.ParseIP returns nil for hostnames
returns nil for any non-IP hostname, so localhost and internal DNS names pass
Basic creds for the registry host attached when a credential exists
non-200 body (size-limited) becomes error text returned to caller

finding.guards_checked: Scheme allowlist (client.go:225-234) passes https and http. Http-downgrade check (client.go:229-230) applies only when the registry is https. IP-literal private/loopback check (client.go:235-242) only covers IP literals. Redirect Authorization stripping (client.go:140-157) does not apply because the realm request is a fresh request. Response size limit (client.go:450-451) applies. Realm return value is checked and used, not discarded. Known gap: alternate IP spellings (e.g. decimal 2130706433) bypass net.ParseIP; whether the OS resolver then reaches loopback is resolver-dependent and was not verified.

finding.claim: Descriptor digests from registry-supplied manifest JSON are interpolated into URL path segments and mount query parameters without validation (digest.Parse/Validate is not called on descriptor digests), so a crafted digest can alter the request path or query on the registry host, with the victim's Authorization attached.
finding.source: Digest strings in manifest/index/subject descriptors from the registry (decoded at registry/remote/repository.go:1215, 1453-1481; registry/repository.go:172-215)
finding.sink: Request URL path for blob GET (repository.go:752-754 via url.go:76-82), manifest GET (repository.go:1114-1116 via url.go:65-71), delete (repository.go:716-722), manifest push (repository.go:1339-1343), and mount query (url.go:94-99)

trace.note: blobStore.Fetch sets ref.Reference from target.Digest.String() with no validation
buildRepositoryBlobURL joins ref.Reference raw into the path
buildRepositoryManifestURL joins ref.Reference raw into the path
buildRepositoryBlobMountURL formats digest and fromRepo into the query unescaped
referrers path decodes registry manifest JSON to read Subject, which feeds descriptors

finding.guards_checked: Reference-string path (registry/reference.go:119-177, repository.go:369-402) validates digests and repository names, and Resolve/Exists/PushReference route through it (repository.go:980, 996, 1164, 1237, 1329), so those are safe. Referrers tag fallback validates via desc.Digest.Validate (referrers.go:108). Descriptor digests on the Fetch/Delete/Push-by-descriptor paths have no validation. Exploitability depends on the server normalizing '..' or '?' in paths, which was not verified. Descriptor sources in the external content/oras packages were not in this subset, so reachability from a remote descriptor to these sinks is UNCERTAIN.
